category_title: High-achieving students who utilize tutoring for collaborative peer-work
minimal_context: The student is in a large math class working on a math project using classroom netbooks.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please open your classroom netbooks and begin working on the math project.

STUDENT: Classes are big, especially math. It’s hard for me to focus and you go fast. I'm going to get out of my seat to go work with my two friends.

TUTOR: Al B, stop getting out of your seat. Everyone in the class is looking at you. Sit down.

STUDENT: I just wanted to work with them. The way they explain work, I really get it.

TUTOR: You need to stay in your seat and do your own work.

STUDENT: (Pushes the netbook away) I'm not doing any more work in class today. And I'm not going to after-school tutoring either.

options.A: Frame the student as a 'mathematician helping professionals'; justify mundane tasks (like formatting netbook entries) by comparing them to professional mathematical standards.
options.B: Allow the student to work with peers to complete math homework and project work on the classroom netbooks.
options.C: Probe the student to consider multiple plausible answers on the math project; deliberately step back from being the single source of knowledge.
options.D: Hold back from providing answers immediately; use careful questioning to respond to student thinking and emphasize conceptual connections on the math project.
